clue.text: In Paris, the first person to anticipate restructuring apt in age?

definitions.text: In Paris, the first person to anticipate restructuring apt in age?

indicators.note: to anticipate is to come before, so the French pronoun is placed ahead of the rest

parts.note: je is the French first-person pronoun, I

indicators.note: restructuring means the letters of apt in age are rebuilt into a new order

explanation.surface: A question about who first foresaw some reorganisation suited to a particular era.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: Jean Piaget, a French-speaking Swiss psychologist, was the pioneer of the idea that a child's thinking is restructured in stages suited to its age.
explanation.definitionFit: Piaget's theory of cognitive development holds that children's understanding is reorganised through stages tied to their stage of growing up.

clue.text: These days out of stock, treasuring old instrument

indicators.note: treasuring means holding something precious within, so one piece is kept inside the other

parts.note: the puzzle appeared in January, so these days are JAN, the current month
NA, not available, is the shop label for goods out of stock

explanation.surface: Nowadays a shop has run out of stock but is hanging on to an antique musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'These days' is topical: the puzzle was published in January. JOANNA is Cockney rhyming slang for a piano.
explanation.definitionFit: In Cockney rhyming slang a piano is a joanna, so the word names a keyboard instrument.

clue.text: Like those from Bow, thus describing school across London?

definitions.meaning: like arrows, which are what a bow shoots
a Cockney, dropping the H, would call Harrow School 'Arrow

explanation.surface: A question about how people from Bow, in London's East End, would describe a school on the far side of the city.
explanation.walkthrough: Bow is an East End district whose natives are traditionally Cockneys, who drop their Hs; Harrow is a famous public school in north-west London.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrowy is an adjective meaning resembling or consisting of arrows, the projectiles fired from a bow.

clue.text: These people dispatched two, so they say, earlier

parts.note: pre is the prefix meaning before or earlier
something dispatched has been sent
the saying goes 'two's company, three's a crowd'

explanation.surface: Some people said to have dispatched a pair earlier, as if gossip about killers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Earlier' supplies PRE, which goes first in the answer even though it comes last in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Present company means the people here now, as in the idiom 'present company excepted'.

clue.text: With a lowering look, can relate

indicators.note: in a down clue, lowering a letter moves it further down the column, later in the word

parts.note: to look is to appear, as in 'he looks tired'
a can is a tin

explanation.surface: Someone with a scowl can still tell a story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lowering look' reads as a scowl, but 'lowering' tells you to move the A of APPEARTIN two places down the column, giving APPERTAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: To appertain is to pertain or belong to something, which is to relate to it.

clue.text: Ten Green Bottles, new title for Archer?

indicators.note: bottles is a verb here: one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: eco is the prefix for environmentally green things
X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: Proposing the nursery song 'Ten Green Bottles' as a new book title for the author Jeffrey Archer.
explanation.walkthrough: Jeffrey Archer, the bestselling British novelist and peer, was jailed for perjury in 2001, so he is a former prisoner.
explanation.definitionFit: Having served a prison sentence, the novelist Archer can be labelled a former convict.

clue.text: What Arab women may wear down Avignon way?

definitions.meaning: an aba is a loose sleeveless robe worn in Arab countries; the plural
in French, the language of Avignon, the cry of protest meaning down with someone is two words, a preposition plus an adverb

explanation.surface: Asking what Arab women might wear as one travels south towards Avignon.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads the answer as two French words, 'à bas', the cry of 'down with'.
explanation.definitionFit: Abas are loose woollen cloaks worn in the Arab world, and 'à bas' is the French protest cry against someone.

clue.text: Shifting Es, these businesses would make bill grow

indicators.note: shifting names letters to be moved to other places in the word
the clue names the letter E, more than one of them, as the letters to be shifted

parts.note: a bird's bill is its beak
to grow is to rise

explanation.surface: A claim that some firms would cause a bill to increase if their Es were shifted.
explanation.walkthrough: Each E moves one place: BEAK becomes BAKE and RISE becomes RIES, so BEAKRISE turns into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Bakeries are shops or firms that bake and sell bread, so they are businesses.

clue.text: This dog's odds double

parts.note: SP, starting price, is the betting odds when a race begins
a ringer is a lookalike or double, as in 'a dead ringer'

explanation.surface: The betting odds on this dog have doubled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Double' looks like a verb about the odds but is a noun for a lookalike.
explanation.definitionFit: A springer is a springer spaniel, a breed of gun dog.

clue.text: Thick-skinned types in shot old book collection entertains

parts.note: hip means fashionable, or in
a shot is a pop, the noise of a gun
OT is the Old Testament, an old collection of books
to entertain is to amuse

explanation.surface: Insensitive people in a photograph keep themselves amused with a library of old books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thick-skinned' reads as insensitive people but is literal: hippos have very thick hides.
explanation.definitionFit: Hippopotamuses have famously thick hides, so they are literal thick-skinned creatures.

clue.text: Perhaps an Athenian's short suit

indicators.note: short means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: an Athenian is an example of a Greek, so perhaps one is a Greek

explanation.surface: An Athenian's suit with short trousers, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' marks an Athenian as just one example of a Greek.
explanation.definitionFit: To suit and to agree both mean to be compatible, as food that does not agree with you.

clue.text: Still a quid? I'm going out for a meal!

definitions.text: I'm going out for a meal!

parts.note: a still is a photograph, a pic
nicker is British slang for a pound, a quid

explanation.surface: Surprise that something still costs only a pound, then an announcement of going out to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: Quid and nicker are both British slang for a pound sterling. The definition is a line a picnicker might say: going outdoors to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: A picnicker is someone who takes a meal outside to eat in the open air.

clue.text: Wales-England river must be filling up by now

indicators.note: filling up means sitting inside and taking up room in the other piece

parts.note: by means near, as in 'stand by the door'
the River Wye forms part of the border between Wales and England

explanation.surface: A river on the Welsh border should have risen by this time.
explanation.walkthrough: The puzzle appeared in mid-January, so the time just now is the New Year. 'By now' looks like one phrase but 'by' is part of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Published in January, the puzzle's present moment is the start of the year.

clue.text: Was H. Burns's film meeting with S. Albright down to her wee producer?

definitions.text: Was H. Burns's film meeting with S. Albright down to her
definitions.meaning: Harry Burns and Sally Albright are the leads in When Harry Met Sally, written by Nora Ephron
a filtering unit of the kidney, which produces urine

explanation.surface: Asking whether a woman was responsible for some film meeting and then a hint about urine.
explanation.walkthrough: Spell out the clue's initials: H. Burns meeting S. Albright is When Harry Met Sally, scripted by Nora Ephron, giving N EPHRON.
explanation.definitionFit: Nephrons are the microscopic filtering units in kidneys, which make urine, or wee.

clue.text: Region organised sports at my place

indicators.note: organised means the letters of sports at are arranged afresh

parts.note: here is where the speaker is, my place

explanation.surface: A local area that has arranged sporting events at the speaker's home.
explanation.definitionFit: The stratosphere is a layer of the atmosphere, a region above the troposphere.

clue.text: For whom, in the absence of blokes, a row's refreshing?

definitions.text: For whom, in the absence of blokes, a row's refreshing?

indicators.note: in means one piece sits within the other

parts.note: nought men, with O for zero, gives O MEN

indicators.note: refreshing means the letters of a row's are made new, in fresh order

explanation.surface: A question: who finds a spell of rowing invigorating when there are no men around?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer: women rowers, with no men in the boat, enjoy a row.
explanation.definitionFit: Oarswomen are female rowers, the crew for whom an outing on the water is the pleasure.

clue.text: Doctor intact having initially lost Amy Pond

indicators.note: having means containing, so the first letters go inside the anagram
to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters of intact are altered
initially means the first letters of the words lost and Amy are taken

explanation.surface: Doctor Who's companion Amy Pond goes missing, but the Doctor remains in one piece.
explanation.walkthrough: Amy Pond is a Doctor Who companion; the definition is only 'Pond', jokey slang for the Atlantic, as in 'across the pond'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pond is informal slang for the ocean between Britain and America.

clue.text: Does motorist observe moon's reflection in it?

definitions.text: Does motorist observe moon's reflection in it?

parts.words: Does motorist observe moon's reflection in it?
parts.note: to moon is to show your bare bottom to someone; a driver ahead of a mooner sees it reflected in the glass that looks backwards

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a driver sees the moon reflected in something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moon' is not the night sky: to moon is to bare your backside, so the reflection is of a rear.
explanation.definitionFit: The driver's mirror shows what is behind the car, which for a mooner is a bare bottom.

clue.text: Tempo for 'Exodus'? A settling standard

parts.note: an exodus is a mass departure, the going
tempo is speed or rate

explanation.surface: A musical question about the pace of something called Exodus, then a phrase about a standard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tempo for Exodus' is a cryptic rendering: the rate of the going.
explanation.definitionFit: The going rate is the usual price, the standard amount paid when settling up.

clue.text: See 17
Nurse what's caught up in zip after this!

indicators.note: caught means held inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: to nurse is to tend

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read upwards, in reverse

parts.note: eh? is a way of saying what? when you have not heard

explanation.surface: A nurse whose clothing got snagged in a zip, ending with an exclamation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Zip' is not a fastener but nothing: after the end there is nothing more.
explanation.definitionFit: The end is the point after which nothing more follows, the final conclusion of a story.

clue.text: When screening for Kung Fu Panda's in respect

indicators.note: screening means shielding something, so the pieces are hidden inside

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I arrived'
pro means in favour of, for
Po is the panda hero of the film Kung Fu Panda

explanation.surface: At a showing of the film Kung Fu Panda.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Screening' looks like a film showing but signals one piece hiding others.
explanation.definitionFit: Apropos means with regard to, concerning, in respect of a matter.

clue.text: This is what's wrong with male fashion

indicators.note: what's wrong with means the letters are out of order and need rearranging

explanation.surface: A complaint about what's the matter with men's clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fashion' is a verb here, to shape, as a smith forges metal.
explanation.definitionFit: To smith is to forge or shape metal, so to fashion it.

clue.text: Wet, just upfront, would like a little spirit

indicators.note: just upfront means taking only the front letter of would

parts.note: an imp is a little spirit, so impish is like one

explanation.surface: Someone damp who would like a small drink of spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wet' is British slang for feeble or weak, not damp; 'spirit' is a sprite, not a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a wet person is ineffectual and feeble, the same as a weakling.

clue.text: Can I hear Test at all? Let me see cycling event

indicators.note: the question asks for what is heard, so the words are taken by their sound

parts.note: test is try, and at all is any, together try any
um is the hesitation noise someone makes while thinking, like let me see

explanation.surface: A cricket fan asks whether any of the Test match can be heard, then pauses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cycling' is not bicycles but recurring: a triennium is a three-year cycle. 'Test' is a cricket Test match in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A triennium is a three-year period, a span that recurs in a regular cycle.

clue.text: Minister to open rally

definitions.meaning: in tennis a ... opens each rally

explanation.surface: A government minister opening a political rally.
explanation.definitionFit: To serve is to attend to people's needs, and in tennis the serve starts the play.

clue.text: Pass around with draught excluder

indicators.note: around means the pass goes round the other letter

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass

explanation.surface: Handing round a strip to stop draughts under a door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draught excluder' suggests a door sausage, but a cowl is a hood on a chimney that keeps draughts out.
explanation.definitionFit: A chimney cowl is a hood fitted to stop wind blowing down the flue.

clue.text: After punch to jaw, flip, face turning scarlet

indicators.note: after means the next piece follows the first

parts.note: to chin someone is to punch them on the jaw

indicators.note: face is the front of the word, and turning swaps its first two letters round

parts.note: to flip is to lose your temper, to see red

explanation.surface: Someone hit on the jaw goes mad and their face goes red.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Face turning' reverses just the first two letters of SEERED to make ESERED.
explanation.definitionFit: Chinese red is a bright orange-red shade, a vivid scarlet colour.
